BRIEF. Application of John Levi Bastian FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF Himself IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT Carlisle, Pennsylvania POST OFFICE ADDRESS OF APPLICANT: Gmil Deloy Tacoma Wash. Date of enrollment, , 190 Term of enrollment, Five (5) years Application for Enrollment in a Nonreservation School. For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Carlisle Pa., of John Levi Bastian, I, John Levi Bastian, of Tacoma P.O., State of Wash., do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to enrollment in said school for a period of years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Pierce County Wash. on July 24, 1888, that the father, Isaac Bastian, a half Indian of the Pugetty Agency; that he left the tribe about three years ago; that the mother, Grilla Bastian, a 1/4 Indian of the Chee Tribe located at Pugetty Agency, and left the tribe about; that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:

This 18th day of January, 1909 Two witnesses: G. Dower Manchester John L. Bastian P.O., Tacoma, Ws (B.S.) NOTE.—Every blank in this application must be properly filled out by the applicant, in his own handwriting, if possible. The signature, whether by mark or otherwise, must be attested by two witnesses. AFFIDAVIT. I, John L. Bastian, do hereby swear that the statements made in the above application are true. Sworn to and subscribed before me this 18th day of January, 1909 NOTE.—This application and affidavit must be executed before some officer authorized to administer oaths by the parent with whom the child is living; if the parents are dead, by the guardian or next of kin. Certificate of Physician. I, C.H. Kinneear, a practicing physician of Tacoma, do hereby certify that I have carefully examined John L. Bastian the child named in this application, and find that he is in proper physical condition to attend school, and is not afflicted with tuberculosis or other disease which would be a menace to the health of other pupils. This 18th day of January, 1909 C.H. Kinneear, M.D. Vouchers of Disinterested Persons. VOUCHER No. 1. I, G. Dowd McIneston, a lawyer at law, of Tacoma, Wn., do hereby certify that I am personally acquainted with John L. Bastian who makes the foregoing application; that I believe his statements therein are true; that I am acquainted with him for ten years; that he is known and recognized in the community with an excellent character; that in my opinion he can not receive proper and adequate schooling at home for the reason that he is beyond the education furnished at Puyallup Bdg. School has no money to complete his course in Tacoma City High School. This 18th day of January, 1909 G. Dowd McIneston VOUCHER No. 2. I, Florence Liston, a former teacher-matron of Tacoma, Wash., do hereby certify that I am personally acquainted with John L. Bastian, who makes the foregoing application; that I believe his statements therein are true; that I am acquainted with him; that he is known and recognized in the community in which he lives as an Indian; and that in my opinion he cannot receive proper and adequate schooling at home for the reason that he has graduated from Puyallup 2nd. Schl. & is now dependent upon his own resources. He is vigorous for a high school boy, but we out of funds. This 18th day of January, 1909 Florence Liston Certificate of School Physician. This __________day of ____________________________, 190________ School Physician. INDORSEMENT. A child showing one-sixteenth or less Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, Indian fashion, who, if debarred from the Government schools, could not obtain an education, may be permitted in the reservation day and boarding schools, but it is preferable that it be not transferred to a nonreservation school, without permission from the Office. Children showing one-eighth or less Indian blood, whose parents do not live on an Indian reservation, whose home is among white people where there are churches and schools, who are presumed to have adopted the white man's manners and customs, and are to all intents and purposes white people, are debarred from enrollment in the Government nonreservation and reservation schools. Superintendents, in all cases where doubt exists as to the degree of Indian blood of a child proposed for transfer, should fully satisfy themselves of the facts by affidavits from reliable persons, which affidavits must be kept on file at the school. A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both Superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and Superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. A pupil dismissed from school for cause must not be enrolled in any other school without the permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Full facts must be submitted with each request.
